title: Quantifying N-Myc and Protein Translation in Neuroblastoma Cells Using Click Chemistry
author: Chittavanich, Saengwimol, et al.
materials:
Timing: 3–5 h
14.Prepare the reagents for Western blot, including 10× tris buffered saline (TBS), immunoprecipitation (IP) lysis buffer, 4× Laemmli sample buffer, 10× running buffer, 5× Tris-glycine buffer, 1× transfer buffer, 1× blocking buffer, and washing buffer (please see recipes for the preparation of Western blot reagents).15.Prepare 10% acetic acid for HRP inactivation. Dilute 50 mL of glacial acetic acid in 450 mL of distilled water in a fume hood. Store at 25°C for up to 3 years.
CRITICAL: Glacial acetic acid is corrosive, flammable, and can cause severe skin burns and eye damage. Keep it from heat sources, wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), and work in a fume hood.
Alternatives: 25 mM glycine-HCl, pH 2.2, supplemented with 1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) can be used.
16.Prepare PVDF membranes (cut to dimensions 8.5 mm x 6.0–7.0 mm) and thick and thin filter papers.

Timing: 1–2 h
17.Prepare 40 mL of 6.0 M NaOH for pH adjustment.a.Weigh out 9.6 g of NaOH and dissolve it in distilled water.b.Adjust the final volume to 40 mL with distilled water in a 50 mL conical tube. Store it at 25°C for up to 3 years.
CRITICAL: Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is a highly corrosive, hygroscopic pellet that can severely burn the skin and eyes. Inhalation may irritate the respiratory system and may cause pulmonary edema. Use appropriate PPE.
18.Prepare 100 mL of 3.74 M tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane (Tris base), pH 8.8.a.Weigh out 45.3 g of Tris base and dissolve it in 40 mL of distilled water.b.While stirring, slowly add approximately 12.3 mL of 37% HCl (12.1 M) until the pH reaches approximately 8.0.c.Adjust the pH to 8.8 by slowly adding 6.0 M NaOH (approximately 14 mL) while stirring.Note: Tris base at pH 8.8 takes a long time to dissolve. We suggest bringing the pH down to 8.0–8.4 by adding concentrated HCl solution and then adjusting to pH 8.8 using NaOH.CRITICAL: Concentrated HCl is highly corrosive and hazardous. Always wear appropriate PPE and work in a fume hood. Use appropriate transfer techniques, such as using a glass pipette. Store HCl in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from incompatible substances.d.Adjust the final volume to 100 mL and store it at 25°C for three years.19.Prepare 40 mL of 1.25 M Tris, pH 6.8.a.Weigh out 6.06 g of Tris base and dissolve it in 20 mL of distilled water.b.Adjust the pH to 6.8 by slowly adding approximately 3.94 mL of 37% HCl.c.Adjust the final volume to 40 mL and store it at 25°C for three years.20.Prepare 40 mL of 10% SDS.a.Weigh out 4.0 g of SDS and dissolve it in distilled water.b.Once completely dissolved, adjust the final volume of the solution to 20 mL with distilled water. Store it at 25°C for up to 3 years.
Note: SDS solutions may become cloudy upon storage, which does not affect the solution's functionality. Warming the solution can resolve the cloudiness.
CRITICAL: SDS causes skin and eye irritation and may cause respiratory irritation. Wear appropriate PPE while weighing.
21.Prepare 20 mL of 10% ammonium persulfate (APS).a.Weigh out 2.0 g of APS and dissolve it in distilled water.b.Once completely dissolved, adjust the final volume of the solution to 20 mL with distilled water.c.Aliquot into 1 mL portions and store at −20°C for up to 1 year.
CRITICAL: APS powder should be kept in a desiccator. Moist air slowly induces APS decomposition, resulting in the loss of its activity. APS is a strong oxidizer. Keep it away from heat sources.

steps.title: Prepare small‑molecule stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make sterile stock solutions of all reagents used for labeling and inhibition, store as indicated.

substeps.instruction: L‑HPG: dissolve 25 mg in 7.64 mL ultrapure water, vortex, filter through 0.22 µm, aliquot, store at 4 °C (≤3 mo) or –20 °C (≤2 yr) to a final concentration of 20 mM.
L‑Methionine: dissolve 25 mg in 8.375 mL ultrapure water, vortex, filter 0.22 µm, aliquot, store as above to 20 mM.
Cycloheximide (CHX): dissolve 10 mg mL⁻¹ powder in cell‑culture‑grade DMSO, vortex; optionally dissolve in ethanol (max 14 mg mL⁻¹). Aliquot, store at –20 °C (≤3 yr).
MG‑132: dissolve 10 mg in 841 µL DMSO, vortex, aliquot, store at –20 °C (≤3 yr) to 25 mM.
TAMRA‑azide: dissolve 1 mg in 1.583 mL DMSO, vortex to 1 mM, aliquot, wrap in foil, store at –20 °C (≤2 yr).
PMSF (0.02 M): dissolve 3.5 mg in 1 mL isopropanol, aliquot, cover with parafilm, store at –20 °C (≤1 yr).

steps.title: Prepare cell‑culture media
steps.instruction: Make all required media solutions, filter‑sterilize, and store at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: 1× PBS: dilute 10× PBS with Milli‑Q water, autoclave.
DMEM/F12 complete: 44.5 mL DMEM/F12 + 5 mL 10× Pen‑Strep + 5 mL 10 % FBS to 50 mL; store ≤1 mo at 4 °C.
RPMI‑1640 for background (L‑Met): 41.75 mL RPMI‑1640 + 0.5 mL 10× Pen‑Strep + 7.5 mL 10 % FBS + 0.25 mL 20 mM L‑Met (final 200 µM).
RPMI‑1640 for labeling (L‑HPG): 41 mL RPMI‑1640 (no Met) + 0.5 mL 10× Pen‑Strep + 7.5 mL 10 % FBS + 0.5 mL 20 mM L‑HPG (final 200 µM).
All media stored at 4 °C ≤1 mo.

steps.title: Set incubator and warm media
steps.instruction: Adjust incubator to 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; pre‑warm all media at 37 °C for 30 min before use.

steps.title: Thaw and passage SK‑N‑BE (2) cells
steps.instruction: Recover cryopreserved cells, remove cryoprotectant, and seed at the recommended density.

substeps.instruction: Thaw vial in 37 °C water bath until a small ice piece remains.
Add 1 mL warm DMEM/F12, transfer to 15 mL tube, add 4 mL DMEM/F12, mix.
Centrifuge 300 g, 4 °C, 5 min; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL DMEM/F12.
Plate 10 mL per T75 flask (or as required).
Maintain cells, changing medium every 3 days; ensure at least one passage before experiment.

steps.title: Prepare Western‑blot reagents
steps.instruction: Make all buffers and solutions needed for SDS‑PAGE and membrane handling.

substeps.instruction: 10× TBS (pH 7.4): dissolve 30.4 g Tris‑base, 87.8 g NaCl, adjust pH with 37 % HCl, bring to 1 L, autoclave, store 25 °C ≤3 yr.

IP lysis buffer (1×): dilute 4 mL 10× TBS to 40 mL, add 0.4 mL NP‑40 (1 % v/v), 1 mM EDTA, 5 % glycerol, bring to 33.5 mL with water; autoclave, store 4 °C ≤2 yr; add 10 µL 100× Halt protease inhibitor per mL before use.

4× Laemmli sample buffer: combine 8 mg bromophenol blue, 1.6 g SDS (4.4 % w/v), 1.2 g Tris‑base (278 mM), 1 mL 37 % HCl, 16 mL glycerol (44.4 % v/v), 16 mL distilled water; bring to 36 mL, store 25 °C ≤3 yr. Add 100 µL β‑mercaptoethanol per mL to make 1× working buffer, store 4 °C ≤1 yr.
10× running buffer: 3.75 g EDTA (0.75 % w/v), 2 % SDS, 10 g Tris‑base (250 mM), 72 g Glycine (1.92 M), bring to 500 mL; store 4 °C ≤2 yr, protect from light.
5× Tris‑glycine buffer: 0.5 g SDS (0.05 % w/v), 30 g Tris‑base (250 mM), 144 g Glycine (1.92 M), bring to 1 L; store 25 °C ≤2 yr.
1× transfer buffer: mix 200 mL 5× Tris‑glycine buffer, 200 mL methanol (20 %), 600 mL water to 1 L; store 4 °C ≤1 yr.
Blocking buffer (1×): 25 g non‑fat dry milk (5 % w/v), 50 mL 10× TBS, 1 mL Tween‑20 (0.2 % v/v), bring to 500 mL; store 4 °C ≤3 mo.
Washing buffer (1×): 50 mL 10× TBS, 1 mL Tween‑20, bring to 500 mL; store 4 °C ≤3 mo.
Acetic acid for HRP inactivation: dilute 50 mL glacial acetic acid in 450 mL distilled water, store 25 °C ≤3 yr.
Cut PVDF membranes to 8.5 mm × 6.0–7.0 mm; prepare thick and thin filter papers.

steps.title: Prepare acrylamide gel reagents
steps.instruction: Make solutions required for casting SDS‑PAGE gels.

substeps.instruction: 40 mL 6.0 M NaOH: dissolve 9.6 g NaOH in water, adjust to 40 mL, store 25 °C ≤3 yr.
100 mL 3.74 M Tris base (pH 8.8): dissolve 45.3 g Tris in 40 mL water, add ~12.3 mL 37 % HCl to pH ≈ 8.0, then add ~14 mL 6.0 M NaOH to reach pH 8.8, bring to 100 mL, store 25 °C ≤3 yr.
40 mL 1.25 M Tris (pH 6.8): dissolve 6.06 g Tris in 20 mL water, add ~3.94 mL 37 % HCl, bring to 40 mL, store 25 °C ≤3 yr.
40 mL 10 % SDS: dissolve 4.0 g SDS in water, bring to 20 mL (note: description says 20 mL, keep as written), store 25 °C ≤3 yr.
20 mL 10 % APS: dissolve 2.0 g APS in water, bring to 20 mL, aliquot 1 mL, store –20 °C ≤1 yr.

steps.title: Plate cells for L‑HPG labeling (Day 0‑5)
steps.instruction: Seed cells at densities that reach 60‑80 % confluence by labeling day.

substeps.instruction: Wash adherent cells once with 4 mL 1× PBS.
Add 4 mL 1× TrypLE Express, incubate 5‑10 min, tap to detach.
Transfer suspension to 15 mL tube, add equal volume PBS, centrifuge 300 g, 5 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL DMEM/F12.
Dilute 5‑10× in a 1.5 mL tube; mix 10 µL diluted cells with 10 µL 0.4 % trypan blue, count viable cells.
For N‑Myc translation assay: plate 2 × 10⁶ cells in 10 mL DMEM/F12 per T75 flask; culture 4 days.
For global protein translation assay: plate 0.3 × 10⁶ cells in 2 mL DMEM/F12 per well of a 6‑well plate; culture 4 days.

steps.title: Prepare labeling media with inhibitors (Day 5)
steps.instruction: Add small molecules to the appropriate RPMI‑1640 labeling media just before treatment.

substeps.instruction: CHX + MG‑132: add 10 µL CHX stock and 10 µL MG‑132 stock per 10 mL L‑HPG RPMI‑1640.
Vehicle + IgG control: add 10 µL DMSO and 10 µL MG‑132 per 10 mL L‑HPG RPMI‑1640.
(-) L‑HPG control: add 10 µL DMSO and 10 µL MG‑132 per 10 mL RPMI‑1640 without L‑HPG.

steps.title: Treat cells with labeling media
steps.instruction: Expose cells to L‑HPG (or control) media for 2 h.

substeps.instruction: Wash cultures twice briefly with 1× PBS.
Add 10 mL labeling media to each T75 flask (or 2 mL to each 6‑well) and incubate 2 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Extract proteins (Day 5)
steps.instruction: Lyse cells in IP lysis buffer, clarify lysates, and quantify protein.

substeps.instruction: Prepare IP lysis buffer containing 1 % Halt protease inhibitor cocktail (add 10 µL 100× per mL).
Wash cells twice with cold 1× PBS.
Add 300–400 µL (T75) or 100 µL (6‑well) IP lysis buffer, incubate on ice 30 min, pipette up/down every 10 min.
Transfer lysate to 1.5 mL tube, centrifuge 4 °C 15 min (speed not specified, assume 14,000 g).
Collect supernatant; store at –80 °C if not used immediately.
Thaw lysates on ice; dilute 10 µL lysate with 10 µL IP lysis buffer (1:1).
Prepare BCA standards: 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2, 1.6, 1.8, 2.0 µg µL⁻¹ BSA in IP lysis buffer.
Add 10 µL of each standard and each diluted sample to a 96‑well plate.
Prepare Pierce BCA reagent (A:B = 50:1) to give 200 µL per well; add 200 µL to each well.
Incubate 37 °C 30 min, read absorbance at 562 nm.
Subtract blank, plot standard curve (zero intercept) to determine sample concentrations.
Aliquot 500 µg protein for N‑Myc assay (store –20 °C) – aim >1 µg µL⁻¹.
Aliquot 10–20 µg protein for global translation assay (store –20 °C).

steps.title: Immunoprecipitate N‑Myc (Day 6‑7)
steps.instruction: Enrich N‑Myc from lysates using anti‑N‑Myc antibody and protein A/G agarose.

substeps.instruction: Thaw protein samples, keep on ice.
Prepare fresh 0.02 µM PMSF in PBS (1 mL per sample).
Dilute lysate to 1.5 µg µL⁻¹: mix 333 µL lysate (≈500 µg protein) with 644.5 µL IP lysis buffer.
Add 2.5 µL anti‑N‑Myc rabbit antibody (1:400) or 2.5 µL rabbit IgG isotype control; rotate 1 h at 4 °C.
Add 20 µL protein A/G plus agarose; final volume ≈1 mL; rotate overnight (14–16 h) at 4 °C on vertical rotator.
Prepare 5 mL IP washing buffer per sample (0.1 % NP‑40, 0.02 µM PMSF, 1× PBS, bring to 25 mL).
Centrifuge 1,000 g 5 min 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Wash beads 4× with washing buffer, repeating centrifugation each time.
Resuspend beads in 50 µL 1× Laemmli sample buffer.
Boil 95 °C 10 min, centrifuge 500 g 5 min.
Transfer supernatant to new tube; store –20 °C until SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Analyze data with Image Lab (Day 12)
steps.instruction: Perform densitometric quantification of nascent N‑Myc and global protein bands using Image Lab software.

substeps.instruction: Open Image Lab, load the immunoprecipitated total N‑Myc image.
Select chemiluminescent panel, open Image Transform, tick “Invert image display”.
Adjust view to single‑image mode.
Use Annotation tools → Text to label lanes and bands.
Close Annotation tools, click “Lane and Bands”, choose “Manual”, enter number of lanes, resize frame to fit membrane.
Click “Bands”, add each band, adjust band region, open “Lane profile”, set background subtraction to 0.7–1.2 mm (≈0.7 mm typical).
Open Analysis Table, display “adj. Volume (int)”, export to Excel.
For nascent N‑Myc: copy lanes/annotations from total N‑Myc file; for negative control lanes create dummy bands of equal width.
Calculate Nascent N‑Myc ratio = (Nascent N‑Myc intensity) / (Total N‑Myc intensity) for each sample or vehicle.
Subtract background using signal from (‑) L‑HPG control.
Compute Relative nascent N‑Myc = Nascent N‑Myc ratio ÷ average ratio of vehicle triplicates.
Perform statistical t‑test on relative values.
For nascent global proteins: open β‑actin image, repeat steps a–h to obtain adjusted intensity.
Open nascent global protein image, repeat steps a–h (set background subtraction to 90.0 mm).
Calculate Nascent global protein ratio = (Nascent protein intensity) / (β‑actin intensity).
Compute Relative nascent global protein = ratio ÷ average vehicle ratio.
Perform statistical t‑test on these relative values.

description: This protocol details the process of quantifying newly synthesized N-Myc and global proteins in SK-N-BE (2) neuroblastoma cells, a model for aggressive neuroblastoma with MYCN amplification, to assess the efficacy of drugs1 or small molecules in inhibiting protein synthesis as a potential therapeutic strategy.2 We introduce an integrated immunoblotting tool to accurately identify and quantify newly synthesized proteins labeled with a clickable amino acid analog, L-homopropargylglycine (L-HPG), enabling their distinction from pre-existing proteins. Our streamlined protocol allows for the Click reaction to occur directly on the polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane, onto which the proteins have been transferred via Western blotting, thus simplifying the procedure compared to others.3 Additionally, we present an optimized Click reaction that leads to an improved signal-to-noise ratio for signal detection, resulting in a ratio greater than 50 for SK-N-BE (2) cells. Moreover, our protocol, incorporating immunoprecipitation (IP), enables the detection of specific protein translation events, such as newly synthesized N-Myc, which cannot be differentiated from pre-existing N-Myc pools using by microscopy,3,4 flow cytometry3,5 or spectroscopy6 for signal visualization. While demonstrated here for neuroblastoma cells, this protocol has also been successfully applied to patient-derived cancer organoids.1,7 We present a simple and cost-effective method for processing up to 28 samples on a single 8.5 cm × 7.0 cm membrane. The protocol comprises six key steps: (1) cell culture and nascent protein labeling, (2) protein preparation, (3) immunoprecipitation assay, (4) Western blotting, (5) Click chemistry reaction on the PVDF membrane, and (6) nascent N-Myc and global protein detection and quantification.
